title: Linkers, Loaders and Program Libraries
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: Which compilation stage converts source characters into tokens?
options: This result cannot be obtained using the stated method.

questions.prompt: In a BST, where is a value less than the current node placed?
questions.answer: In its left subtree (under the chosen no-duplicate convention).
options: In its left subtree (under the chosen no-duplicate convention).
In its right subtree (under the chosen no-duplicate convention).
There is not enough information to determine the result.
questions.feedback: Model answer: In its left subtree (under the chosen no-duplicate convention).

questions.prompt: Why can an array provide direct indexed access?
questions.answer: Its element locations can be calculated from base address and index.
options: Its element locations can be calculated from base address OR index.
Its element locations cannot be calculated from base address and index.
Its element locations can be calculated from base address and index.
questions.feedback: Model answer: Its element locations can be calculated from base address and index.

questions.prompt: A full adder receives A=1, B=1 and carry-in=0. What are sum and carry-out?
options: Sum -1 and carry-out 1.
Sum 0 and carry-out 1.
Sum 1 and carry-out 1.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: linker — Resolves symbols and combines object modules.
loader — Places an executable in memory ready to run.
dynamic linking — Resolution/use of shared code at load time or runtime.

blocks.title: Compile modules
blocks.text: Source files become object modules with symbols/references.

blocks.title: Link dependencies
blocks.text: Linker resolves symbols and combines modules/libraries; static/dynamic linkage differs.

blocks.title: Load and run
blocks.text: Loader maps executable and needed libraries into memory, then begins execution.

blocks.title: Worked example · Model answer
blocks.text: Compile source modules into object files; linker resolves the call and produces linked executable (or dynamic references); loader places executable and required libraries in memory and starts execution. Check: link each claim to the scenario and use precise OCR terminology.
